official_sources.finding: gdalbuildvrt builds mosaics from ordered input rasters; input order is material to overlap resolution.
Without a pixel function, files listed later have priority in overlap areas.
Source nodata can cause data to be fetched from a lower-priority overlapping dataset.
Alpha is not generally alpha-composited in gdalbuildvrt overlap priority, so alpha=0 may still override lower content unless mask behavior is used.
Starting with GDAL 3.3 source mask bands are used by default through UseMaskBand when building VRTs.
-ignore_srcmaskband disables source-mask participation and allows the last source to override earlier sources in overlap.
-srcnodata writes NODATA into ComplexSource elements and can override intrinsic source nodata semantics.
-vrtnodata defines output VRT nodata independently of input nodata.
Areas inside VRT extent but outside every source read as valid zero unless VRT nodata or alpha is explicitly configured.
-addalpha marks uncovered VRT areas transparent with alpha 0 and covered areas opaque with alpha 255.
gdal raster mosaic defaults to resolution=same and errors if source resolutions differ.
highest, lowest, average and common resolution policies produce different target grids and must be pinned.
common resolution uses a greatest-common-divisor style source-pixel dimension rule.
Target-aligned-pixels rounds output extent so extent coordinates divide evenly by target resolution.
gdal raster mosaic records relative input paths by default when possible, so path base is part of replay provenance.
Starting with GDAL 3.12 a mosaic pixel function such as min, max, mean or median changes overlap semantics from source priority to explicit aggregation.
Without an overlap pixel function, gdal raster mosaic uses input-list order for priority and later inputs win.
VRT SimpleSource explicitly binds SourceFilename, SourceBand, SrcRect and DstRect.
SrcRect and DstRect are pixel/line rectangles whose geospatial meaning depends on source and VRT geotransforms.
SourceFilename relativeToVRT controls whether a relative source path is resolved against the VRT file.
ComplexSource can mask source data using NODATA or UseMaskBand before transforming values.
ComplexSource mask use is binary; it does not imply continuous alpha blending.
A VRT SourceBand may explicitly refer to a source mask band, making mask source identity auditable.
GTI virtual mosaics support explicit overlap z-order through SORT_FIELD.
GTI SORT_FIELD_ASC controls whether overlap sort priority is ascending or descending.
GTI honours mask and alpha bands when compositing overlapping tiles, unlike classic VRT alpha-compositing limitations.
GTI can reproject tiles with different SRS on the fly, so terminal terrain work must reject an unmanifested mixed-SRS mosaic path.
GTI RESAMPLING applies when tile origins are not aligned to the mosaic resolution grid, making alignment drift a value-changing operation.
GTI relative filenames are resolved relative to the tile-index path.
gdaltindex can persist per-tile filename and footprint and is suitable as GTI source lineage.
For GTI, explicitly setting target resolution and datatype is recommended instead of inferring them from the first tile.
GTI tile indexes should explicitly declare nodata and mask when tiles use them.
A GTI tile index may fetch raster metadata such as pixel size or creation date into index fields for lineage checks.
Warp/reproject nodata and masks are excluded from interpolation according to the selected resampling kernel.
UNIFIED_SRC_NODATA policy changes multi-band nodata validity behavior and has version-dependent defaults.
Target-aligned-pixels during reprojection can alter the requested extent and blank edge trimming behavior.
gdal raster info exposes raster size, CRS, geotransform, block size, nodata, unit and checksum for source-tile identity manifests.
gdal raster compare can compare pixels, CRS, geotransform, overviews and metadata against a golden mosaic.
gdalcompare reports pixel-level differences and supports golden-image replay of seam windows.
gdal_merge also gives later input images precedence in overlap and treats nodata on a per-band basis.
VRT multithreaded RasterIO optimizations are constrained to non-overlapping sources, underscoring that overlap paths are semantically distinct.
Raster block size is an access/storage property and must not redefine logical pixel identity at tile seams.
